extracted.intended_audience: Current Contents readers, librarians, publishers, and ISI/production staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practical criteria for designing and producing weekly Current Contents editions (covers, binding, typography, contents/indexing, and distribution) to maximize durability, legibility, scanability, bibliographic utility, and cost-effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover construction: separate cover vs self-cover
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace the old 'self-cover' (same paper as inside leaves) with a 'separate cover' made of heavier, more durable stock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate cover "allows CC to circulate with a minimum of wear and tear" and "will not only last for many years, but it also feels great." Self-covers were chosen originally for cost and time savings, but separate covers improve durability and perceived quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding type: use perfect binding when page count requires
rubrics_metrics.description: Switch from saddle-stitch (staples) to 'perfect' (glued) binding for editions whose page count exceeds saddle-stitch limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perfect binding allows flexibility to increase the number of pages (e.g., CC/LS grew from ~30 pages to ~320+). Other CC editions will continue to be bound with staples unless size requires perfect binding. Perfect binding glues the stack to the spine and is more durable for large issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covers should be informative (highlight featured items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design covers to be more informative by highlighting titles of Citation Classics and Current Comments essays, which change week-to-week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placing titles of essays and commentaries on the covers will help readers, administrators, and librarians quickly locate a specific work; the redesign aims to make this information prominent and useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominent edition identification on the back edge
rubrics_metrics.description: Print volume, number, and date of each CC issue in large, easy-to-read type along the back edge of the edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This makes it easier to locate and differentiate various CC editions when shelved or stacked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inside front cover: include ordering/contact and purpose information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a complete, succinct inside-front-cover section listing how to obtain articles, who to contact with questions, how to order CC worldwide, and a statement of CC's purpose and weekly features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include information such as how to obtain articles via OATS/Sci-Mate and other online systems; this improves user access and reduces confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents page legibility and scanability (borderlines and new type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve contents pages by adding borderlines at the top and bottom of each page and lines above and below each journal title, and by setting standard volume/issue info in new, clearer type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Borderlines and clearer type are intended to help users scan CC faster; some journals may appear several per page—layout aids should make it easier to find where a specific journal begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain essential bibliographic identifier (oval number)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain the existing 'oval' number used to identify each journal issue; do not change this identifier used for ordering and for OATS/Sci-Mate access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The oval issue number is essential for ordering articles through ISP's Original Article Text Service (OATS) and for online retrieval systems; it must remain unchanged to preserve interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate overlapping coverage across CC editions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark journals that are covered in more than one CC edition so subscribers who receive multiple editions can avoid duplicate scanning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new feature will add special codes to bibliographic entries to indicate multi-edition coverage, helping subscribers quickly see when a journal appears in more than one edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid problematic vertical black bars; prefer alternative delineation
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate the black vertical bars previously used to separate disciplines on the page because they caused problems in binding and trimming; use horizontal delineation instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vertical bars sometimes showed through after trimming or were lost during saddle-stitch binding. Horizontal lines and other layout approaches better accommodate multidisciplinary journals and binding tolerances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect multidisciplinary journal placement and category integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept that the system of categorizing journals is inherently multidisciplinary and avoid rigid attempts to force single-discipline placement that compromise readers' expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers value integrity of their subject disciplines; redesigns should be sensitive to how journals cross categories and avoid surprising changes that alienate professional readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase type size in author/address directories for legibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Enlarge author/address directory type (example: from four-point to four-and-one-half-point) to improve readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increasing type size required >25% more area and added pages to accommodate larger type; production procedures must be adjusted (and page counts accepted) to improve usability for librarians, secretaries, and readers who rely on small reprint/address cards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify address listing procedures to include necessary address detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan procedural modifications to address listings (e.g., include street addresses where necessary) to improve the usefulness of the address directory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to how addresses are formatted and listed may be required in future printings; procedural changes should be implemented without compromising bibliographic utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use back cover for ads and subscription cards when feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the back cover for advertisements and subscription-card inserts to save envelope cost and mailing labor where postal regulations permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is feasible in the US and can reduce costs and labor (mailing without envelopes), but international postal regulations vary, so universal implementation is not guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider international postal regulations in production choices
rubrics_metrics.description: When changing mailing/cover practices (e.g., inserting cards, mailing without envelopes), verify that methods comply with postal regulations of every destination country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because CC is mailed worldwide, production and mailing practices must be tested for international acceptability before broad rollout; something feasible in the US may not work elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain cost-effectiveness while improving features
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement improvements in a manner that balances benefits with cost; strive for enhancements that are cost-effective and sustainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal of the changes is to 'improve CC in a cost-effective manner.' The publisher acknowledges costs will increase for some changes (e.g., larger type, more pages) but emphasizes avoiding unnecessary cost increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage design experts and balance innovation with familiar imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult outside and internal design experts and balance visually attractive prototypes with the need to retain a familiar, recognizable layout for readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several prototype covers were prepared; the staff compromised to retain the familiar image of CC while incorporating many recommended design improvements (e.g., inside front-cover info, cover highlighting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear ordering and access pathways (OATS, Sci-Mate, online systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure articles in CC remain linkable to ordering and online retrieval systems (e.g., OATS, Sci-Mate) and make those pathways clear in the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All CC articles are available online through Sci-Mate and other online systems; the redesign emphasizes including information to order/download items and to use personal online access where available.
